sentences.text: The claimant on the other hand contends that the finding regarding involvement of the vehicle cannot be found fault with.
It is also contended that the sums awarded are on the lower side.

4. The evidence on record indicates that immediately after the claimant suffered an accident, he was shifted to Dhanvanthari Hospital and from there, he was taken to St. Martha's Hospital and was actually accompanied by the Police.
5.
The evidence on record also indicates that MLC was registered but the name of the claimant had been wrongly shown as Dhanvanthary Hospital.

But subsequently, in the MLC register of the St.
Martha's Hospital, the name was correctly registered.
6. In light of the fact that an MLC was registered, it cannot be contended that an accident did not occur nor can it be stated that no vehicle has been involved.
The argument that there was delay of six days in filing the FIR was itself sufficient to come to the conclusion that the vehicle has not involved, cannot be accepted.
7. It is to be noticed that the claimant was aged 78 years and was hospitalized immediately after the accident.
Since MLC was registered, the claimant HAD actually had no obligation to file a FIR.
However, subsequently, he has filed a FIR and the owner of the vehicle had arrayed as respondent No.2.
He did not deny the occurrence of the accident.
Further more, the charge sheet laid against the driver of the offending vehicle belonging to respondent No.2.
8. The Tribunal taking into consideration all these factors has come to the conclusion that mere delay in filing the FIR cannot be a ground to reject the claim of the claimant.
I cannot find any fault with reasoning of the Tribunal and thus, the appeal of the insurer is therefore, dismissed.
9. As far as compensation is concerned, no medical evidence is adduced to indicate that any permanent disability suffered of the claimant.

It is however, seen that the claimant had suffered fractures and hence, the award of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' is inadequate and would have to be enhanced to Rs.60,000/.
10.

Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.20,000 /- as against the sum of Rs.11,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
11. The sums awarded under the heads of medical expenses and loss of income during laid up period awarded by the Tribunal are just and proper and do not call for modification and hence confirmed.

12. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Compensation under different by the by this No.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.1,06,664/- as against Rs.77,664/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
14. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
15. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
16. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
17. The appeal of the claimant is accordingly allowed in part.
